campaigns.name: The 90-Second Dare
campaigns.objective: awareness — show skeptical podcasters exactly how fast podclip works by making the render time the hero of the story
campaigns.big_idea: Drop a real-time screen recording: upload a 60-minute episode, hit go, watch the clip set land in 90 seconds. No voiceover needed — the clock does the talking. Seed it on X and YouTube Shorts where podcasters already scroll.
campaigns.hook: I uploaded a 60-minute episode. Here's what happened 90 seconds later.

sample_copy.headline: 90 seconds. A full episode. A clip set ready to post.
sample_copy.body: No timeline scrubbing. No guessing which moment lands. podclip's hook-detection model — trained on 40,000 manually rated clips — finds the moments worth sharing and renders them, captioned and framed, before your coffee cools. Watch the whole thing happen in real time.

assets_needed: Screen-recorded demo video of a real upload-to-clips workflow timed to 90 seconds
X post thread with timestamp screenshots
Reddit post with honest context and link to demo
campaigns.success_metric: Number of free signups in the 72 hours after posting
campaigns.why_on_brand: Leads with the outcome before the feature, names the pain (timeline scrubbing, guessing), and lets a concrete proof point do the heavy lifting — exactly the DNA's 'outcome first, dry confidence' playbook.

campaigns.name: Bad Clip Hall of Fame
campaigns.objective: community — build rapport with podcasters by roasting the generic auto-clipper problem they already hate
campaigns.big_idea: Invite podcasters to share the worst auto-generated clip they ever got from a competitor — the random 60-second window that starts mid-sentence and ends on dead air. Curate the funniest submissions in a weekly thread. podclip's hook-detection angle writes itself without a single feature bullet.
campaigns.hook: Show me the worst auto-clip you've ever received. I'll start.

sample_copy.headline: Generic auto-clippers have given us some real gifts.
sample_copy.body: Mid-sentence cuts. Clips that open on 'um.' Sixty seconds of someone pouring water. We've all been there. Drop your worst auto-clip horror story below. We're collecting them — partly for science, mostly for catharsis. podclip exists because nobody should have to post that.
sample_copy.cta: Share your worst. Then try the alternative.

assets_needed: Seed post with a real (or clearly labeled mock) bad-clip example
Response template for engaging with submissions
Weekly recap graphic of top submissions
campaigns.success_metric: Thread replies and quote-posts in the first 48 hours
campaigns.why_on_brand: Uses dry humor and self-aware asides to build rapport, names the pain before the solution, and trusts the reader to connect the dots — core DNA dos.

campaigns.name: Show Your Clips
campaigns.objective: signups — turn podclip's existing 120 weekly shows into social proof by spotlighting real clips in the wild
campaigns.big_idea: Feature one clip per week from a show already using podclip — no testimonial copy, just the clip itself with a one-line caption crediting the show. The clip quality is the pitch. Rotate across X, LinkedIn, and the podclip site's showcase page.
campaigns.hook: This clip came out of a 60-minute episode. podclip found it.

sample_copy.headline: Real shows. Real clips. No editor required.
sample_copy.body: Every week, 120 shows use podclip to turn full episodes into clips worth sharing. This one's from [Show Name]. The hook-detection model flagged it. The caption style was already set. The host just posted it. That's the whole workflow.
sample_copy.cta: See what podclip finds in your episode.

assets_needed: Permission emails to featured show hosts
Clip export files from participating shows
Branded one-line caption template for each post
campaigns.success_metric: Click-throughs to the signup page from showcase posts week-over-week
campaigns.why_on_brand: Proof comes only from observed proof points (120 weekly shows), leads with outcome, uses active second-person voice — respects the DNA's 'outcome before feature' and 'no invented metrics' rules.

campaigns.name: The Clipping Hour
campaigns.objective: community — build a recurring touchpoint with indie podcasters by hosting a live teardown of what makes a clip actually shareable
campaigns.big_idea: A monthly 30-minute live session on X Spaces or LinkedIn Audio where the podclip team plays three clips — one great, one mediocre, one bad — and explains what the hook-detection model looks for. No sales pitch. Just craft talk that podcasters actually want.
campaigns.hook: What makes a podcast clip actually worth sharing? Let's find out live.

sample_copy.headline: We're playing three clips. You tell us which one lands — then we'll tell you why.
sample_copy.body: Every month we pull three real clips, strip the show names, and break down what makes one shareable and another forgettable. It's the same judgment call our hook-detection model makes — trained on 40,000 manually rated clips. Come argue with us. Bring your own examples.
sample_copy.cta: Set a reminder. First session is free to attend (they all are).

assets_needed: X Spaces or LinkedIn Audio event setup
Three clip examples (anonymized or with permission)
Post-session recap newsletter draft
Reminder post 24 hours before each session
campaigns.success_metric: Live attendees per session, growing month-over-month
campaigns.why_on_brand: Addresses the audience as peers who care about craft, uses dry confidence without overselling, and builds on the 40,000-clip proof point as a credibility anchor.

campaigns.name: Launch on Product Hunt — The Honest Way
campaigns.objective: signups — reach early-adopter creators and indie hackers who influence podcaster tool choices
campaigns.big_idea: A Product Hunt launch that leads with the hook-detection angle and the 90-second render stat — no hype, just the two facts that make podclip different from every other clipper. The maker comment does the heavy lifting with a candid explanation of why generic scene detection fails.
campaigns.hook: Auto-clippers pick random moments. We trained a model on 40,000 manually rated clips to find the ones worth sharing.

sample_copy.headline: podclip — hook-detection for podcasts, not random 60-second windows
sample_copy.body: Every other clipper cuts your episode into chunks and hopes one lands. podclip's model was tuned on 40,000 manually rated clips to find narrative tension — the moment a listener would actually share. Upload a 60-minute episode. Get a branded clip set in about 90 seconds. Three clips free, no card required.
sample_copy.cta: Try it on your next episode.

assets_needed: Product Hunt listing copy and tagline
Demo GIF or short video showing upload-to-clips flow
Maker comment explaining the hook-detection model in plain language
Outreach list of podcaster communities to notify on launch day
campaigns.success_metric: Upvotes and free signups on launch day
campaigns.why_on_brand: Direct, no-hype framing with proof points front and center — matches the DNA's 'lead with outcome, name the pain, trust the reader' approach and avoids every forbidden phrase.

campaigns.name: Show HN: We Trained a Clip-Selection Model on 40k Rated Clips
campaigns.objective: awareness — reach technical founders and indie hackers who influence tool adoption and can amplify the model-quality story
campaigns.big_idea: A Show HN post that explains the actual problem with generic scene detection, how the training data was assembled, and what the model looks for — written as a builder talking to builders. No marketing copy. The comments become the distribution.
campaigns.hook: Show HN: podclip — we rated 40,000 podcast clips by hand to teach a model what's actually worth sharing

sample_copy.headline: Show HN: podclip — we rated 40,000 podcast clips by hand to teach a model what's actually worth sharing
sample_copy.body: Generic auto-clippers use scene detection or fixed windows. We wanted something that understood narrative tension — the moment a listener leans in. So we rated 40,000 clips manually and trained on that signal. The result: a 60-minute episode becomes a branded clip set in about 90 seconds. Happy to talk about the model, the data pipeline, or why FFmpeg is both a gift and a curse.
sample_copy.cta: Try it free — three clips, no card.

assets_needed: HN post draft with honest builder framing
Prepared responses to likely technical questions (model architecture, data labeling process, render pipeline)
Link to a public demo or loom walkthrough
campaigns.success_metric: HN points and number of comments in the first 6 hours
campaigns.why_on_brand: Candid, direct, zero jargon — the DNA's conversational confidence applied to a technical audience that rewards honesty over polish.

confidence.notes: Brand DNA is from Descript (a competitor/adjacent tool), not podclip's own site — voice calibration is an approximation based on APP_PROFILE.voice and DNA tone_words applied to podclip's context. Proof points used are from APP_PROFILE.proof_points only; no additional claims invented. No numeric claims appear beyond the three stated proof points.
